headline: Denied request to amend conditions at 421 Main Street; continued front yard fencing rules and 461 Boston Road parking plan.
summary: The petitioner for 139 Paramount Street asked to move its junk yard and vehicle storage permit to October. A slaughterhouse business for chickens at 785 Page Boulevard, called a neighborhood butcher shop, will be heard first at the October hearings meeting. Speakers on both sides of the front yard fence amendment were heard before councilors voted to continue it.
decisions: Continued parking plan change at 461 Boston Road and ES Morton Street, 9-1, with one abstention.
Denied request to amend conditions for the special permit at 421 Main Street, 4-7.
Continued front yard fencing amendment to Article 7, Section 7.4.23(A), 10-1.
Moved the 785 Page Boulevard slaughterhouse business review to the first item at the October hearings meeting.

decision_evidence.quote: COUNCILOR EDWARDS MADE A MOTION TO CONTINUE AND IT WAS SECONDED BY COUNCILOR FENTON.
PRESIDENT WHITFIELD STATED THIS WILL BE HEARD FIRST IN THE OCTOBER HEARINGS MEETING.

decision_titles: Parking plan at 461 Boston Road and ES Morton Street
Amended conditions for special permit at 421 Main Street
Front yard fencing amendment, Article 7, Section 7.4.23(A)
plain_text:
City Council  
     
Regular Meeting 
 
~Final~ 
   
 
36 Court Street  
Springfield, MA 01103   
http://www.springfieldcityhall.com 
 
Gladys Oyola-Lopez 
 
September 28, 
2026 
6:30 PM City Hall - Room 200 
 
 
 
Roll Call 
COUNCILORS WALSH, DAVILA AND BROWN WERE REMOTE FOR THIS MEETING. 
 COUNCILOR FENTON ARRIVED AT 6:40 PM.  COUNCILORS HURST AND DELGADO 
WERE ABSENT. 
Moment Of Silence - Pledge Of Allegiance 
 
Special Permits 
 1. 139 Paramount Street - Junk Yard/Vehicle Storage Operation 
PETITIONER ASKED TO BE MOVED TO OCTOBER MEETING FOR MORE TIME TO 
MEET WITH RESPECTIVE NEIGHBORHOOD COUNCIL. 
 2. 461 Boston Road & ES Morton Street — Change in parking plan 
RYAN MCCOLLUM PRESENTED THE CHANGE IN THE PARKING PLAN.  THIS 
WOULD ALIEVIATE THE PARKING ISSUES AT EMBER BY ADDING ANOTHER 20 
SPOTS.  COUNCILOR GOVAN ASKED FOR CLARIFICATION. 
COUNCILOR CLICK BRUCE SUPPORTS WITH THE CONDITION THAT THE 
COMPANY COMES BACK IN FRONT OF THE NEIGHBORHOOD COUNCIL.  THE 
NEIGHBORHOOD HAS RECOMMENDATIONS. 
COUNCILOR WALSH SUPPORTS THE CONTINUATION. 
 
AYES Brian Santaniello, Maria Perez, Kateri Walsh, Victor Davila, Zaida 
Govan, Michael Fenton, Lavar Click-Bruce, Melvin Edwards, Tracye 
Whitfield 
NAYS Gerry Martin 
AWAY None
RECUSE None 
ABSTAIN Malo Brown 
ABSENT Justin Hurst, Jose Delgado 
 
  
 3. 421 Main Street & SS Main Street (IO) - Amending Conditions 
ED SHVETSOV OWNER PRESENTED AMENDMENTS TO THE SPECIAL PERMIT THAT 
WAS CONTINUED FROM AUGUST.  PHIL DROMEY STATED THAT THE 
COMMERCIAL PROPERTIES CANNOT HAVE RESIDENTIAL TRASH BARRELS.   
COUNCILOR GOVAN DID A SITE VISIT ON 9/23.  SHE STATED THERE HAS BEEN 
MISCOMMUNICATION BETWEEN THE BUSINESS AND THE CITY.  THINKS THE 
COUNCIL SHOULD SUPPORT. 
COUNCILOR EDWARDS STATED THAT PAST PERFORMANCE MATTERS.  HAS NO 
INTENTION IN SUPPORTING THIS SPECIAL PERMIT.  OPERATING A CAR BUSINESS 
WITHOUT A DUMPSTER IS UNREASONABLE.  HAD PHIL DROMEY SPEAK ON THE 
HISTORY OF VIOLATIONS AT THIS SITE. 
THIS SPECIAL PERMIT WAS DENIED. 
 
AYES Maria Perez, Zaida Govan, Kateri Walsh,Tracye Whitfield 
NAYS Brian Santaniello, Gerry Martin, Malo Brown, Victor Davila, Michael 
Fenton, Lavar Click-Bruce, Melvin Edwards 
AWAY None 
RECUSE None 
ABSTAIN None 
ABSENT Justin Hurst, Jose Delgado 
 
 
  
 
Zone Changes 
 4. Amending Article 7, Section 7.4.23(A) — Fencing 
COUNCILOR MARTIN ASKED TO TAKE THIS ITEM OUT OF ORDER WITH NO 
OBJECTION.  PHIL DROMEY FROM PLANNING INTRODUCED THE AMENDMENT 
FOR FRONT YARD FENCING.   
COUNCILOR MARTIN WANTS THE ORDINANCE TO BE FAIR FOR SINGLE FAMILY 
HOMES. 
PROPONENTS OF THE ORDINANCE SPOKE ON THE MATTER.
OPPONENTS OF THE ORDINANCE SHARED THEIR REMARKS ON THE MATTER. 
PROPONENTS AND OPPONENTS HAD AN ADDITIONAL 5 MINUTES. 
COUNCILOR GOVAN SHARED A STORY OF HER CONSTITUENTS AND READ HER 
STATEMENT.  SHE ASKED PHIL IF THERE IS A DISABILITY WAIVER IN THE 
PROPOSAL AND HE SAID THERE IS NOT.  THERE IS A FORM IN THE LAW 
DEPARTMENT FOR RESIDENTS CAN APPLY FOR.   
COUNCILOR BROWN THANKED COUNCILOR MARTIN FOR PROPOSING THE 
AMENDMENT.  HE ACKNOWLEDGED THAT COMMUNICATION WITH RESIDENTS 
NEEDS TO BE BETTER.  HE IS IN SUPPORT DUE TO HAVING A BIG FAMILY AND 
PETS. 
PHIL DROMEY STATED THAT THERE IS NO CLARIFICATION ON FENCE TYPES. 
COUNCILOR MARTIN RECOGNIZED SCHOOL COMMITTEE MEMBER, BARBARA 
GRESHAM.  HE ECHOED THE REMARKS OF THE PROPONENTS.  BELIEVES THIS TO 
BE A COMMON SENSE CHANGE. 
COUNCILOR WALSH APPRECIATES THE RESIDENTS CONCERN OF FAMILY 
SAFETY.  SHE IS IN SUPPORT OF THE AMENDMENT.  THINKS THE FEES BE 
ELIMINATED.  PHIL STATED THE RATES ARE SET BY THE REPUBLICAN.  
COUNCILOR CLICK-BRUCE IS IN SUPPORT OF THIS MATTER.  REFERENCED A 
PERSONAL EXAMPLE OF THE PROTECTION OF A FENCE.PHIL STATED THAT 
FENCES CAN GO UP TO THE PROPERTY LINE. 
COUNCILOR DAVILA CLARIFIED THAT THE HISTORIC DISTRICT HAS TO GO IN 
FRONT OF THE HISTORIC COMMISSION.   
COUNCILOR EDWARDS APPRECIATES BOTH SIDES OF THIS MATTER.  HE SHARED 
A PERSONAL STORY ABOUT NOT HAVING A FENCE.  THINKS THERE SHOULD BE 
MORE DISCUSSION ON THIS ISSUE. 
COUNCILOR EDWARDS MADE A MOTION TO CONTINUE AND IT WAS SECONDED 
BY COUNCILOR FENTON. 
COUNCILOR FENTON SAID BOTH SIDES HAVE GREAT ARGUMENTS.  
AYES Brian Santaniello, Gerry Martin, Maria Perez, Malo Brown, Zaida 
Govan, Kateri Walsh, Victor Davila, Lavar Click-Bruce, Melvin 
Edwards, Tracye Whitfield 
NAYS Michael Fenton 
AWAY None 
RECUSE None 
ABSTAIN None 
ABSENT Justin Hurst, Jose Delgado 
 
 
  
 5. Amending Springfield Zoning Ordinance Article #'s 2, 4, 5, 7 & 9
M.G.L. Chapter 111, Section 151 – Slaughter House Review/Consent  
 6. 785 Page Boulevard - Slaughterhouse Business 
ATTORNEY RYAN O'HARA OF BACON & WILSON SPOKE ON BEHALF OF 
PETITIONER ADEL SAEED ON THE PROPOSAL "A NEIGHBORHOOD BUTCHER 
SHOP" 
COUNCILOR SANTANIELLO CLARIFIED THAT THIS WAS JUST FOR CHICKENS.   
COMMISSIONER CAULTON - HARRIS THE VOLUME OF DELIVERY IS A CONCERN, 
AND WILL THERE BE OTHER RETAIL ITEMS FOR SALE.  CHICKENS CAN ONLY BE 
CAGED ON SITE FOR NO MORE THAN 2 WEEKS.  INSPECTIONS WILL BE 
FEDERALLY REGULATED WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF THE EMPLOYEES. 
 COMMERCIAL HVAC WOULD REGULATE ODORS INSIDE THE BUILDING.   
THERE WAS AN OBJECTION MY COUNCILOR BROWN TO CONTINUE THE MEETING 
PAST 9:30. 
PRESIDENT WHITFIELD STATED THIS WILL BE HEARD FIRST IN THE OCTOBER 
HEARINGS MEETING. 
[MIN_SIGNATURES]
